title: Persuading
job: Make a case, concede a point, hold your ground
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: present, for the claim and the concession alike
imperfetto, L2-M10's, for dicevo — what you were in the middle of saying
the bare infinitive, after ti conviene, vale la pena and è difficile

rules.text: THE CONCESSIVE MOVE IS A STRUCTURE, NOT A WORD. È vero che X, ma Y. Hai ragione, però Y. D'accordo, però Y. The first half really does give ground — it is not a politeness formula — and the ma or the però is what turns it into a move instead of a surrender. Everything you actually want said goes in the SECOND half. A speaker who concedes and then trails off has agreed, whatever they meant.

ITALIAN HAS TWO WORDS FOR but AND POSITION SPLITS THEM. ma can only OPEN its clause. però can open it or CLOSE it: Hai ragione, però non lo faccio, and equally Hai ragione, non lo faccio però. The final però is the one that sounds Italian and the one no learner produces without being told; it lands lighter than the fronted version, closer to English though at the end of a sentence. ma at the end is not possible.

conviene IS A FALSE FRIEND TWICE OVER. It is not convenient and it is not agreeable: it means it is in your interest. It also runs IMPERSONALLY, like piacere and mi serve — the thing that suits you is the subject, and you are the indirect object: ti conviene aspettare, mi conviene partire, gli conviene prenotare. There is no io form of it in this use.

THE PERSUASIVE REGISTER IS GRADED, WHERE ENGLISH HAS ONE should. dovresti (L3-M4) is friendly advice between equals. ti conviene appeals to the listener's own interest and is the least pushy of all, because it claims nothing about what is right. sarebbe meglio is impersonal and hides the speaker. devi (L3-M2) is an order. Choosing the wrong rung of that ladder is what makes a reasonable case sound like a demand.

THE ADVICE FAMILY TAKES A BARE INFINITIVE, SO NO MOOD IS NEEDED AT ALL. ti conviene aspettare, vale la pena provare, basta chiedere, bisogna partire. This is how Italian gives somebody a reason to act without going near the congiuntivo, and it is why this module comes before the mood rather than after it. Nothing between the phrase and the infinitive: never ti conviene di aspettare.

sentences.display: È vero che costa di più, ma dura molto
sentences.cue: It is true that it costs more, but it lasts a long time
sentences.literal: Is true that it-costs of more, but it-lasts much

words.note: The concession, said whole. It hands the point over honestly, and the clause after ma is where your own case goes. Never è vero che sia.
From durare, regular -are. Used of things that wear well and of events that run long: il film dura due ore.

sentences.trap: è vero che takes the ordinary indicative — costa, not costi. The congiuntivo appears after doubt, and conceding a point is the opposite of doubting it.
sentences.sound: e VE-ro ke KO-sta dee PYOO, ma DOO-ra MOL-to. è is the open e of the copula, and it carries its accent in writing.

variations.display: È vero che costa di più, però dura molto
variations.cue: It is true that it costs more, though it lasts a long time
variations.changed: però for ma, slightly softer

variations.display: Costa di più, è vero, ma dura molto
variations.cue: It costs more, true, but it lasts a long time
variations.changed: the concession moved inside as an aside

variations.display: È vero che costa molto, ma dura di più
variations.cue: It is true that it costs a lot, but it lasts longer
variations.changed: the comparison moved to the second half

mistake.display: È vero che costi di più, ma dura molto
mistake.why: è vero che is not a doubt trigger, so it takes the indicative costa. costi would be the congiuntivo, and it is wrong here.

sentences.usage: Arguing for the more expensive option without pretending it is cheap.
sentences.mnemonic: Concede in half one, argue in half two.

sentences.display: Hai ragione, però non ho tempo adesso
sentences.cue: You are right, but I do not have time right now
sentences.literal: You-have reason, however not I-have time now

words.note: Italian HAS reason where English IS right, so the verb is avere. L3-M3's bare ragione is the same noun inside penso di avere ragione.
The second but. Unlike ma it can also close the clause: Hai ragione, non ho tempo però. That final position is the one worth practising.

sentences.trap: Sei ragione is not Italian. Being right, being hungry and being cold all run on avere, and this is the phrase where the habit gets fixed.
sentences.sound: eye ra-JO-ne, pe-RO non o TEM-po a-DES-so. però is stressed on the final o and carries the accent in writing, which distinguishes it from nothing else but marks the stress.

variations.display: Hai ragione, non ho tempo adesso però
variations.cue: You are right — I do not have time right now, though
variations.changed: però moved to the end, which ma cannot do

variations.display: Hai ragione, però adesso non ho tempo
variations.cue: You are right, but right now I do not have time
variations.changed: adesso fronted inside the second half

variations.display: Hai ragione, ma non ho tempo adesso
variations.cue: You are right, but I do not have time right now
variations.changed: ma for però, a shade blunter

mistake.display: Hai ragione, non ho tempo adesso ma
mistake.why: ma cannot close a clause. Only però can sit at the end; with ma the sentence has to be Hai ragione, ma non ho tempo adesso.

sentences.usage: Accepting somebody's point while declining to act on it today.
sentences.mnemonic: però can end a sentence; ma cannot.

sentences.display: Ti conviene prenotare adesso, costa molto meno
sentences.cue: You are better off booking now, it costs a lot less
sentences.literal: To-you it-suits to-book now, it-costs much less

words.cue: you are better off, it is in your interest
words.note: Impersonal like mi piace: the listener is ti, and a bare infinitive follows. The most persuasive and least pushy way to give advice.
Regular -are, used for tables, tickets and rooms alike. La prenotazione is the booking itself.

sentences.trap: conviene is not convenient. It says the thing is in your interest, usually financially, and a speaker who reads it as convenient will use it for the wrong half of an argument.
sentences.sound: tee kon-VYE-ne pre-no-TA-re a-DES-so, KO-sta MOL-to ME-no. conviene has the ie glide, kon-VYE-ne.

variations.display: Ti conviene prenotare adesso
variations.cue: You are better off booking now
variations.changed: the reason dropped, leaving the bare advice

variations.display: Conviene prenotare adesso, costa molto meno
variations.cue: It is worth booking now, it costs a lot less
variations.changed: no ti, so the advice is to nobody in particular

variations.display: Ti conviene prenotare prima
variations.cue: You are better off booking in advance
variations.changed: prima for adesso, so it is about habit

mistake.display: Ti conviene di prenotare adesso, costa molto meno
mistake.why: Nothing goes between conviene and the infinitive. It is ti conviene prenotare, exactly as it is vale la pena provare.

sentences.usage: Pushing somebody to act now by appealing to their wallet rather than to your preference.
sentences.mnemonic: conviene = it suits YOU, not me.

sentences.display: D'accordo, però almeno dobbiamo partire presto
sentences.cue: All right, but at least we have to leave early
sentences.literal: Of-agreement, however at-least we-must to-leave early

words.note: Marks the minimum you will settle for, which is exactly what a concession needs next. It sits in front of the thing conceded to.

sentences.trap: L2-M6's d'accordo settled a time; here the same word concedes a point. The apostrophe is part of the word and it is never written d' accordo or da accordo.
sentences.sound: dak-KOR-do, pe-RO al-ME-no dob-BYA-mo par-TEE-re PRE-sto. d'accordo runs together, dak-KOR-do.

variations.display: D'accordo, però dobbiamo partire presto
variations.cue: All right, but we have to leave early
variations.changed: almeno dropped, so the demand is flat

variations.display: Hai ragione, però almeno dobbiamo partire presto
variations.cue: You are right, but at least we have to leave early
variations.changed: hai ragione for d'accordo as the concession

variations.display: D'accordo, però almeno dobbiamo partire adesso
variations.cue: All right, but at least we have to leave now
variations.changed: adesso for presto: a time, not a habit

mistake.display: Sono d'accordo però almeno dobbiamo partire presto
mistake.why: Not wrong, but it is a different move: sono d'accordo agrees with the position, while bare d'accordo only accepts the point and keeps the argument open.

sentences.usage: Giving way on the plan while holding on to the one condition you care about.

sentences.display: Vale la pena provare, secondo me
sentences.cue: It is worth trying, in my view
sentences.literal: It-is-worth the trouble to-try, according to-me

words.note: One block, and then a bare infinitive. Literally it is worth the trouble. The di version, vale la pena di provare, is heard too, but the bare one is commoner in speech.
Regular -are. It covers trying something out and trying clothes on, and it is the verb this whole advice family reaches for.

sentences.trap: pena is trouble here, not pain or penalty. Nobody hears anything grim in vale la pena; it is as light as English worth a go.
sentences.sound: VA-le la PE-na pro-VA-re, se-KON-do me. vale is stressed on the first syllable, VA-le.

variations.display: Secondo me vale la pena provare
variations.cue: In my view it is worth trying
variations.changed: the opinion fronted

variations.display: Vale la pena provare, non costa molto
variations.cue: It is worth trying, it does not cost much
variations.changed: a reason instead of an opinion

variations.display: Non vale la pena provare
variations.cue: It is not worth trying
variations.changed: negated, and the whole block stays intact

mistake.display: Vale la pena che provo, secondo me
mistake.why: vale la pena takes an infinitive, not a clause. Adding che pulls the sentence towards a mood the module does not need: vale la pena provare.

sentences.usage: Recommending a low-stakes experiment when the other person is hesitating.
sentences.mnemonic: vale la pena + infinitive, nothing between.

sentences.display: In realtà non è così caro, anzi conviene
sentences.cue: Actually it is not that expensive — on the contrary, it is a good deal
sentences.literal: In reality not is so dear, on-the-contrary it-suits

words.note: Corrects an assumption the other person has made. Unlike English actually it is never a filler, so it always signals a real correction ahead.

words.cue: on the contrary, in fact even
words.note: Goes further than the correction before it: not merely not expensive but positively good value. English has no single word for it.

words.cue: it is worth it, it pays
words.note: The bare impersonal, with nobody named. Said of a price or a plan it means it is the sensible buy.

sentences.trap: anzi does not mean but. It never contradicts your OWN previous clause; it strengthens it, so the half after anzi must go further in the same direction.
sentences.sound: in re-al-TA non e ko-ZEE KA-ro, AN-tsee kon-VYE-ne. anzi has the ts sound, AN-tsee.

variations.display: In realtà non è caro, anzi conviene
variations.cue: Actually it is not expensive — on the contrary, it is a good deal
variations.changed: così dropped, so the claim is absolute

variations.display: Non è così caro, anzi conviene provare
variations.cue: It is not that expensive — in fact it is worth a try
variations.changed: an infinitive after conviene

variations.display: In realtà conviene, non è così caro
variations.cue: Actually it is a good deal, it is not that expensive
variations.changed: the two halves swapped, so the verdict leads

mistake.display: In realtà non è così caro, anzi è molto caro
mistake.why: anzi must push further in the same direction, not reverse it. For a reversal the word is ma or però.

sentences.usage: Rescuing an option the other person has already written off on price.
sentences.mnemonic: anzi doubles down, ma turns round.

sentences.display: Comunque il mio punto di vista non cambia
sentences.cue: Anyway, my point of view has not changed
sentences.literal: Anyway the my point of view not changes

words.note: Returns to your position after a detour, which is the move that keeps a concession from becoming a retreat. It opens or closes the clause.
Three words, one idea, and the plural moves only the first: punti di vista. Il mio punto di vista keeps the article before mio.
Regular -are, and it works with or without an object: la situazione cambia, cambio idea.

sentences.trap: Italian keeps the article in front of a possessive: il mio punto di vista, not mio punto di vista. Only single family nouns drop it, which is L2-M2's rule.
sentences.sound: ko-MUN-kwe il MEE-o POON-to dee VEE-sta non KAM-bya. comunque is ko-MUN-kwe, with the qu said kw.

variations.display: Comunque il mio punto di vista è questo
variations.cue: Anyway, this is my point of view
variations.changed: stated positively instead of as an unchanged fact

variations.display: Il mio punto di vista comunque non cambia
variations.cue: My point of view, in any case, has not changed
variations.changed: comunque moved inside, where it sounds calmer

variations.display: Comunque non cambia niente
variations.cue: Anyway, nothing changes
variations.changed: the subject dropped for a flat close

mistake.display: Comunque mio punto di vista non cambia
mistake.why: The article is compulsory before mio here: il mio punto di vista. Dropping it is the mistake L2-M2's family rule invites.

sentences.usage: Closing a round of argument without conceding the substance.
sentences.mnemonic: comunque brings you back to your point.

sentences.display: Insomma, è difficile convincere mio padre
sentences.cue: In short, it is hard to convince my father
sentences.literal: In-short, is difficult to-convince my father

words.note: Sums up what has been said and signals you are landing. On its own, with a shrug, it also means so-so — but at the head of a clause it is a summary.
One form for both genders; only the plural moves, to difficili. Stressed on the second syllable, dif-FEE-chee-le.
The -ere verb behind this whole module. Its participle is irregular, convinto, and the person convinced is a direct object.

sentences.trap: Bare Insomma with a shrug answers how was it? and means not great. At the front of a clause it is the summary word, and tone alone separates the two.
sentences.sound: in-SOM-ma, e dif-FEE-chee-le kon-VEEN-che-re MEE-o PA-dre. convincere has two soft c sounds, kon-VEEN-che-re.

variations.display: Insomma, è difficile convincere mia madre
variations.cue: In short, it is hard to convince my mother
variations.changed: mia madre, so the possessive agrees the other way

variations.display: È difficile convincere mio padre, insomma
variations.cue: It is hard to convince my father, in short
variations.changed: insomma at the end, summing up after the fact

variations.display: Insomma, convincere mio padre è difficile
variations.cue: In short, convincing my father is hard
variations.changed: the infinitive fronted as the subject

mistake.display: Insomma, è difficile convincere il mio padre
mistake.why: Single family nouns drop the article after a possessive: mio padre, mia madre. il mio padre is the L2-M2 rule broken.

sentences.usage: Wrapping up a long complaint about somebody who will not be moved.
sentences.mnemonic: insomma at the front sums up.

sentences.display: Appunto, è quello che dicevo prima
sentences.cue: Exactly — that is what I was saying earlier
sentences.literal: Precisely, is that which I-was-saying earlier

words.note: Claims the other person has just made your point for you. It is agreement used as an argument, and it is very common in real disputes.
The imperfetto of dire, for something you were in the middle of saying. Its participle detto is L3-M5's.

sentences.trap: appunto is not merely yes. It says the point you just made is the one I already made, which is why it can sound sharp if the other person had not meant to agree.
sentences.sound: ap-POON-to, e KWEL-lo ke dee-CHE-vo PREE-ma. appunto holds the double p, ap-POON-to.

variations.display: Appunto, è quello che dicevo
variations.cue: Exactly — that is what I was saying
variations.changed: prima dropped, so it is about right now

variations.display: Appunto, è quello che dicevo prima io
variations.cue: Exactly — that is what I was saying earlier
variations.changed: io added at the end for emphasis on who said it

variations.display: È appunto quello che dicevo prima
variations.cue: That is precisely what I was saying earlier
variations.changed: appunto moved inside as an adverb

mistake.display: Appunto, è quello che ho detto prima
mistake.why: Not wrong, but it changes the move: ho detto reports a finished statement, while dicevo says you were in the middle of making the point all along.

sentences.usage: Pouncing, politely, when somebody arrives at the position you started from.
sentences.mnemonic: appunto = you have just proved my point.

sentences.display: Soprattutto ti conviene parlare con lui
sentences.cue: Above all, you are better off speaking to him
sentences.literal: Above-all to-you it-suits to-speak with him

words.note: Ranks one reason above the rest, which is what a case needs at the end. Two t's in the middle, from sopra plus tutto.

sentences.trap: parlare takes con for the person spoken to, not a. parlare a exists in careful writing, but con is what is said.
sentences.sound: so-prat-TOOT-to tee kon-VYE-ne par-LA-re kon LOO-ee. the double t is held twice over: so-prat-TOOT-to.

variations.display: Ti conviene parlare con lui, soprattutto adesso
variations.cue: You are better off speaking to him, especially now
variations.changed: soprattutto moved to the end, ranking the timing

variations.display: Soprattutto ti conviene parlare con mio padre
variations.cue: Above all you are better off speaking to my father
variations.changed: the person named instead of a pronoun

variations.display: Soprattutto, conviene parlare con lui
variations.cue: Above all, it is best to speak to him
variations.changed: ti dropped, so the advice is general

mistake.display: Sopratutto ti conviene parlare con lui
mistake.why: The word carries two t's in the middle: soprattutto. One t is the commonest spelling error Italians themselves make.

sentences.usage: Landing the strongest reason last, when the other arguments have not moved anybody.
